Aroer by the Arnon
uh-ROH-er by the AR-non
proper noun
Hebrew ‘arō‘ēr, “ruins” or “bare height,” with Arnon, “rushing stream”; the border city standing upon the very brink of the river Arnon.

Biblical Definition

Aroer by the Arnon was the southern border city of the Amorite kingdom of Sihon, perched upon the rim of the deep gorge of the river Arnon. When the LORD delivered Sihon before Israel, the conquest is measured “from Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon” (Deu 2:36); there was not one city too strong, for the LORD gave all into Israel’s hand. The land from Aroer was granted unto the Reubenites and the Gadites (Deu 3:12), and the inheritance of Reuben is marked again “from Aroer, that is upon the bank of the river Arnon” (Josh 13:16). Joshua records how Sihon “ruled from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the river Arnon” (Josh 12:2). In the day of Moab’s calamity Jeremiah calls upon her: “O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done?” (Jer 48:19). This Aroer is to be distinguished from the Aroer before Rabbah given to Gad, and from the Aroer of Judah. It is a frontier stone, set where the river divides the land. Let it remind the believer that the LORD setteth the bounds of habitation (Deu 32:8); the borders of the nations and the lines of our heritage fall by His appointment, and the inheritance of His people is no chance possession but a gift of His covenant hand.

Webster 1828 Definition

The border city upon the brink of the river Arnon, frontier of the Amorite kingdom, given to Reuben in Israel’s inheritance.

AROER BY THE ARNON, the city standing upon the very brink of the deep gorge of the river Arnon.

The name signifies “ruins” or “bare height,” and it marked the southern frontier of Sihon the Amorite.

It became the boundary of the inheritance given to the tribe of Reuben.

It is to be distinguished from the Aroer of Gad before Rabbah and the Aroer of Judah.

It witnesses that the LORD setteth the bounds of habitation and divides the inheritance of His people.

Key Scripture

Deu 2:36 — "From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the LORD our God delivered all unto us:"

Deu 3:12 — "And this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, and half mount Gilead, and the cities thereof, gave I unto the Reubenites and to the Gadites."

Josh 12:2 — "Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and from the middle of the river, and from half Gilead, even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;"

Jer 48:19 — "O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done?"

Modern Corruption

A border place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that the LORD setteth the bounds of the nations and divides the inheritance of His people.

expand to see more

Aroer by the Arnon is a frontier city of the sacred record, named where the river divides the land and the inheritance of Reuben begins. No movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it; the dictionary marks it that the reader may know it for a real boundary in a real land, distinct from the other Aroers of Gad and Judah.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the providence of God over the bounds of habitation (Deu 32:8; Act 17:26). He who fixed the lip of the Arnon as a border, and gave the cities thereof to His people, orders still the lines that fall to us; the heritage of the saints is no accident of history but the appointment of a covenant-keeping God.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “ruins” or “bare height,” Aroer names the city set upon the brink of the river Arnon.

expand to see more

Aroer by the Arnon — Hebrew ‘arō‘ēr, “ruins” or “bare height.”

It stood upon the very brink of the deep gorge of the Arnon.

It marked the southern border of the Amorite kingdom of Sihon.

It fell to the tribe of Reuben in the dividing of the land.

It is distinct from the Aroer of Gad before Rabbah and the Aroer of Judah.

Usage

"Like Aroer set upon the brink of Arnon, the bounds of every people are fixed by the hand of God."

"The believer’s inheritance falls in pleasant places by the appointment of the LORD, not by chance."

"Stand by the way and ask what is done, that the judgments of God upon the nations be not forgotten."
